propositions: when a git push is rejected by policy (hook declined, branch protection), the rejection reason is captured by run_git but discarded before being logged, causing the failure to appear as a transient retry-exhausted message rather than naming the actual cause

rejected push failures are not retried correctly: the broad _NON_FF substring classifier catches policy rejections (which contain 'rejected') and misroutes them onto the retry path instead of the terminal path, causing up to three wasted fetch-merge cycles

a diverged tickets branch accumulates unpushed commits silently: PUSH_PENDING is computed only in fsck (pull-only) and never consulted by write paths, so an eight-hour outage with 122 unpushed commits remained invisible until a manual git push forced discovery

ticket event payloads (comments, raw environment output) are never scanned for secrets on write; gitleaks only scans code at the review gate, leaving credentials routinely pasted in comments undetected
async push policy and library embedders receive no warning of a rejected push: stderr=DEVNULL on detached Popen and NullHandler on library use make failures completely undeliverable
